newsitem.title: UK: BA says engineering arm sparks interest.
newsitem.headline: BA says engineering arm sparks interest.

text.p: British Airways said Sunday that it had received several approaches from companies wishing to invest in its engineering arm but insisted it was too soon to speculate on when an announcement would be made.

The Sunday Times reported that General Electric of the United States was thought to have made tentative approaches to buy a big stake in the division in a deal that could value the business at about 600 million pounds ($1 billion).
But a spokeswoman for BA said: "It is early to speculate on anything." She declined to say how many companies had come forward or whether GE was a potential partner.
Bob Ayling, BA's chief executive, said last September that he wanted to convert BA Engineering into a separate company and explore a third party investment, with BA retaining a majority stake.
"Since then, approaches have been made by a number of interested parties," the spokeswoman added.

BA Engineering employs 9,000 people. It was converted into a separate profit centre in 1995 with the aim of increasing its independence from the main airline operations and already provides services for over 100 other airlines.
